entries.what: Independent report, photograph or video of surfable waves on the Airwave in December 2019 (the developer's claim 'successfully created peeling waves')
entries.where: web searches 2026-10-05/10 across ABC, Tracks, Bunbury Mail, South Western Times, RWR, Swellnet forum; Waveco's About page (R21)
entries.by: agent: Bunbury source check and 3D agents (cloud)
entries.detail: ABC (2019-12-16) reports only the tear and paraphrases a tourist 'looking forward to riding whatever wave'; no independent photo, video or report of surfable waves exists. Waveco's own account is self-published, says 'In 2018' (the installation was attempted in December 2019 and the bladder was removed within about three days), and Bottegal's Zoom interview of 8 Oct 2026 is unrecorded personal communication. So the card keeps the verdict FAILED.

entries.what: Google Earth / Esri imagery of the Airwave in the water (9-20 December 2019) and Esri Wayback release 4756 (2019-12-12)
entries.where: https://wayback.maptiles.arcgis.com (release 4756 tile); Esri World Imagery -33.327276, 115.629902; Google Earth Pro history
entries.detail: Release 4756 is labelled 2019-12-12 but its imagery at this spot dates from 2016-03-03, i.e. before the reef (tile removed). The current Esri image (2025-08-30) shows the real site (Bunbury Back Beach SLSC) with no trace of the structure; the nearest imagery found at the site is 2016 and 2025. The bladder sat in the water only about 9-16 Dec 2019, so only an image from that week could show it. The position (about 45 m off the low-tide mark, just south of the surf club) is text only, +-100 m alongshore.
entries.might_work: Google Earth Pro historical imagery for 9-20 Dec 2019 (Lior: G3 / A1-A4 in the Bunbury 3D requests)

entries.what: As-installed record of the bladder: dive log, photos with a scale, as-installed height (1.6 m or 2.0 m), cross-section, fill level when the seam tore; RWR original un-cropped drone frames
entries.where: Waveco (Troy Bottegal), City of Bunbury December 2019 council papers, Raised Water Research
entries.detail: Not found anywhere online. The 12 m diameter and 1.6 m height are text (Tracks 2019-11-15); the planform drawing is a regular circle, so the size agreement is by construction. The drone photo (RWR) and ABC video frame carry no scale or georeference. Claude never sends e-mail.
entries.might_work: Lior: E5 (Waveco / City of Bunbury) and E6 (RWR drone frames with metadata)

entries.what: Local tide gauge, post-2009 bathymetric survey and measured wave data at Bunbury Back Beach
entries.where: WA Department of Transport survey index; GHD 2021 tide planes (Bunbury Port gauge, inner harbour about 3 km NE of Back Beach)
entries.detail: No local gauge found at Back Beach (Bunbury Port planes assumed to apply on the micro-tidal open coast); the only seabed survey is the WA DoT 2009 airborne lidar (10 m grid, 10 years before the install, cannot resolve a 12 m reef; the 67 MB .bag was not re-downloaded). Navionics SonarChart matches it only after reading depths below LAT (RMS 0.32 m) and does not show the structure.
entries.might_work: Lior: E7 (WA Department of Transport) for any later survey; Navionics app readings B1-B11

entries.what: Planned second Airwave prototype (December 2020), the planned 12-month UWA study and any later Airwave installation
entries.where: South Western Times 2020-07-09; Tracks 2021-10-08; Bunbury Mail 2022; waveco.com.au (2025)
entries.by: agent: Bunbury card research and 3D agent (cloud)
entries.detail: No source confirms that the December 2020 second installation took place or succeeded, that the inflatable was ever reinstalled after December 2019, or that the 12-month University of Western Australia study ever started (no results found). By 2025 Waveco's public Bunbury project appears to be a different (granite) design. The cost is disputed between sources (about US$350,000 vs US$400,000); only the A$75,000 council contribution is corroborated.

entries.what: Gemini's Bunbury sources and shape: ABC .../airwave-artificial-surf-reef-bursts-bunbury-back-beach/11802958, ABC image 'airwave-torn-bladder-bunbury-2019.jpg', Bottegal (2019) 'Airwave Project Brief', 'Surfer Magazine Bunbury Airwave Trial Review (2020)', Wikimedia Back Beach photos
entries.where: Gemini dossier and images_provenance.json (read-only); the named URLs fetched 2026-10-05
entries.detail: The ABC URL returns 200 but id 11802958 is an unrelated ABC Listen item (Townsville floods); the real article is .../word-first-surf-reef-tears-during-installation/11803228. The ABC image URL is 404. The Wikimedia Back Beach photos are generic beach photos from 2006 and 2021 and do not mention Airwave. The Brief and the Surfer Magazine review were not found (Surfer was on hiatus 2020 to Aug 2024). Gemini's 24-gon footprint (113 m2) is a formula, its coordinates (-33.3362, 115.6261) are about 1 km south of the real site, and its helical anchors, 130 t, crest 1.8 m and hemispherical dome are contradicted or unsupported. Gemini lead not confirmed; nothing used.
